harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented an Ansible-based nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data (node2) to /var/backups/inventory (node1) with 7-day retention, orchestrated from node3 (the only node with Ansible installed, hence the control_node), scheduled via a nightly cron entry on node3. Verified the backup, retention, and post-reboot recovery on all three nodes.
actions_performed: Established SSH trust: added CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY to authorized_keys on node1 and node2 for the antrieb user with passwordless sudo

Discovered node1/node2 are RHEL7 with only Python 2.7 (no python3, no package repos), incompatible with ansible-core 2.20's Python3-only module execution; switched to the `raw` module for all remote operations to avoid requiring a target-side Python interpreter
Created representative /srv/inventory/data content on node2 (warehouse-a.csv, warehouse-b.json) since the source path did not previously exist
Wrote /root/ansible/inventory-backup/inventory.ini defining node2 (source) and node1 (dest) groups with ansible_user=antrieb and the cluster ed25519 key

Wrote /root/ansible/inventory-backup/backup.yml: play 1 (node2) tars /srv/inventory/data, base64-encodes it, registers the content as a fact, and cleans up the temp archive; play 2 (node1) ensures /var/backups/inventory exists, decodes/writes the dated archive, and prunes all but the 7 newest inventory-data-*.tar.gz files
Wrote /root/ansible/inventory-backup/schedule.yml which uses Ansible's cron module to install a nightly (02:00) root crontab entry on node3 that runs `ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini backup.yml`
Ran backup.yml manually, verified the archive was correctly written and extractable on node1 with the exact source content
Seeded 9 synthetic aged backup files on node1 and re-ran backup.yml to prove retention trims to exactly the 7 newest archives

Executed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol sequentially on node1, node2, and node3: captured boot_id/service/data baseline, issued native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and confirmed recovered service/data state on each
After node3's reboot, re-ran backup.yml end-to-end to prove full functional recovery of the Ansible control node and its SSH key/crontab

evidence.requirement: Nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data (node2) to /var/backups/inventory (node1), implemented via Ansible
evidence.summary: backup.yml created and executed via ansible-playbook; archive written to /var/backups/inventory on node1 and verified byte-identical to source via tar extraction
Seeded 9 aged archives (mixed with real backup) then re-ran the playbook; listing shows exactly 7 archives remain, oldest 3 pruned
schedule.yml used Ansible's cron module to install a root crontab entry on node3 (02:00 daily); crond confirmed active
Baseline boot_id 33b0e84c captured with backups/sshd healthy; reboot acked; node polled back; boot_id changed to 73467be7 with sshd active and all 7 backups intact
Baseline boot_id 95e2f83d captured with source data/sshd healthy; reboot acked; node polled back; boot_id changed to a13424be with sshd active and source data intact

Baseline boot_id e796da36 captured with cron active and crontab/playbook files present; reboot acked; node polled back; boot_id changed to 31bd68fd with cron active, crontab intact, and a full end-to-end ansible-playbook backup run succeeding post-reboot
